text.p: These are the leading stories in the Malawi press on Friday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Polling in Blantyre's by-election proceeded quietly on Thursday as police maintained a heavy presence in anticipation of violence after a last minute opposition boycott.
- Fifteen pregnant women from Zomba district hospital marched on parliament to protest against the lack of hospital services affected by a civil service strike.
- Seventeen people were arrested for cheating during a by-election in central Blantyre on Thursday where less than five percent of registered voters participated in the poll.
- Two British teachers from Lilongwe were killed by unknown attackers as they were returning to Malawi from Mozambique.
